name: fail-closed-schema-digest-approval
description: V0 campaign-controller schema pattern: rejectUnknownKeys everywhere, approval digest over canonical JSON (recursively key-sorted) so binding is key-order-independent, timestamps normalized to ISO UTC before digesting, validation clock injected via nowMs for deterministic tests, committed data profiles validated against a FixedClock pinned near fetchedAt

name: admission-boundary
description: Admission boundary pattern (warren-a252): import keys campaigns by canonical manifest digest; approveCampaign re-states the exact digest+approver; admitWorkItem runs all invariants fail-closed (expiry, policy freshness+digest, ordered membership, upstream allowlist, mutation flags, warren identity, campaign+daily budget, concurrency, one active attempt) and only then reserves per-run budget in one store.transaction. Refusals are AdmissionRefusal with a stable invariant discriminator; untrusted issue text can only cause refusals; no client import so no network can precede admission.

name: openclaw-v0-e2e-acceptance
description: The OpenClaw V0 e2e acceptance scenario (extensions/campaign-controller/src/acceptance/openclaw-v0.e2e.test.ts) proves the full fake-server vertical slice: committed profiles import, one dispatch, PR-intent render, duplicated/reordered page ingestion, controller+Warren restart, and stable single state. Dry-run no-mutation is a structural property: assert recorded fake-GitHub methods are GET/HEAD and no token reaches durable payloads. Operator boundary published in extensions/campaign-controller/RUNBOOK.md.

title: Phase 3: response loop via ephemeral follow-up runs on the PR branch; all repo behavior as profile data
rationale: Long-lived/extended-TTL run pods were rejected: they idle-burn budget and fight the ephemeral-run model. Fresh journaled follow-up runs dispatched onto the existing PR head branch give the same result with bounded, per-intent-auditable cost. Repo-agnosticism is the exit hatch if openclaw proves too costly a target.

name: phase3-mutation-flags
description: Phase-3 mutations (warren-094b) extend the enforced-by-absence pattern per flag: one transport class per mutation, constructible only from a policy with that individual flag true, intents verified against policy upstream coordinates, journaling via shared executeJournaledMutation (planned-before-I/O, canonical digest, pr_execute-identical transitions). Extending EXECUTABLE_MUTATION_FLAGS is the reviewable schema event; widening MUTATION_FLAGS requires touching profile JSON + test policy literals because fixtures bind every flag explicitly.

name: amendment-flow-in-place
description: Manifest amendments (warren-35c4) apply IN PLACE on the campaign row rather than creating a new digest row: amendment document references campaignId + baseManifestDigest, carries only appendIssues/budget/prompt/maxConcurrentRuns/expiresAt, and its own approval envelope becomes the new manifest's approval envelope; validateCampaignManifest is re-run over the composed manifest so all invariants (digest binding, cap layering, expiry) hold for free. No superseded attention row is emitted. Planned never-executed actions are invalidated (permanent_failure/policy_violation, reservation released); executing ones stay with the dispatcher. Note: check:dups scans extensions/campaign-controller/src too — keep CLI command functions thin by extracting shared helpers.
